transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. ...Well, I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to slow down. Since I stopped working, I mean. 

I'm always up and moving around, going from one little job to the next all day. Just... acting like I still have a crew waiting on me or something. That's about it.
How has your sleep been lately?
My sleep? It's... fine, I guess. I get enough. Nothin' really to report there.
Have you always been this way, or is this something that only started recently?

Well... I don't know about always. But it only became a real problem recently. After I retired, I mean. I was doing handyman work for a long time... gave that up about a year and two months ago, I guess. That's when it started getting to be an issue.
When you are keeping busy like that, do you feel a sense of dread or worry that something bad will happen if you don't stay occupied?
No... no dread or anything. I just... I just like to keep moving. Nothin' bad's gonna happen, I just don't like sitting still.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory or your ability to keep track of things since you retired?

I mean... maybe a little. Just normal stuff, I figure. Sometimes I don't get around to returning calls from the community center. Or... well, my wife has to remind me to pay a bill now and then. Left some supplies at home that I told the garden group I'd bring... stuff like that. Just little things.
Have these recent memory slips or lapses in keeping track of things ever caused you to get lost or led to any significant problems with your daily safety?
No. Nothin' like that. I know my way around just fine. Haven't gotten lost or... left the stove on or anything dangerous. Just... forgetting a call or a bill, like I said.
Do you feel that these memory slips are a noticeable change from how your memory was when you were still working?
Not really. I've... I've always been a bit like that, I guess. Just forgetting little things here and there. I don't think it's much different now than it was back then.
Do you find that you still enjoy the activities you used to, or do you feel a sense of sadness or emptiness that has been weighing on you lately?
No, no sadness or anything. I still like the garden group... still like doing my own thing. I feel fine.
When you are moving from one task to the next all day, do you feel an internal sense of pressure or a restless urge that makes it difficult for you to choose to sit down and relax?

I suppose. I don't know about pressure, really. But... if I have to sit through a quiet meeting, or church or something, I just feel like I've got to shift around. Tap my foot, or... get up and stretch. Even when I know I should just stay put. It's just hard to sit still sometimes.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you struggle to sit still or find yourself constantly fidgeting back then as well?

I suppose so. It's been a long time, but... yeah. Back in grade school, my teachers used to say I was bright, just... scattered. Always losing my pencils, or blurting out answers out of turn. They always had to remind me to actually finish my work before I took off for recess. So... yeah, I guess it was like that back then, too.
